trial_court: Family Court, Bhawanipatna, C.P. No. 31 of 2014
case_name: These Matters Are Taken Up By Video ... vs Bhawanipatna In Part So Far As The ...

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Appellant-husband (MATA No. 102 of 2015) and Appellant-wife (MATA No. 182 of 2015)

facts_of_case: The parties filed a joint compromise petition for dissolution of their marriage under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act. The trial court dissolved their marriage on mutual consent without any permanent alimony to the wife as well as cost of the litigation.

legal_principles.principle: A court may award permanent alimony to a wife even if she has not claimed any maintenance.
legal_principles.held: The Court below thought it appropriate to award permanent alimony of Rs.8,00,000/- to be paid to the wife towards her maintenance as well as the maintenance and future prospect of her daughter.

legal_principles.principle: A husband has a duty to maintain his wife even if she has no financial interest over him.
legal_principles.held: The Court below thought it appropriate that the duty of the husband petitioner to maintain his wife although she has no financial interest over him.

legal_principles.principle: A court may consider the financial status of a husband when awarding alimony to his wife.
legal_principles.held: The Court below observed that the husband being a businessman having status, standard and prosperity in the society who can afford the maintenance of his daughter in the custody of the wife.

outcome.final_order: The final court order modified the direction for payment of Rs.8,00,000/- to the wife towards her maintenance and education.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
